Kanawana 


KAMP _KANAWANA 1975 


DIRECTOR'S REPORT 


INTRODUCTION 


The elghty-second year of Kamp Kanawana has come to an end. It 
Is our objective to provide programs that will encourage the 
growth and development of young people in an outdoor setting. It 
Is very exciting and often dramatic to see the positive change In 
people at Kanawana. This leads to the bellef that we are attaln- 
Ing our goals for operation. 


Kamp Kanawana '75 has been the best year of the past three years. 
Our kampers benefited greatly by thelr experiences thls summer. — 
This report Is Intended to give an honest Impression of this year 
as well as to recognize areas requiring Improvement or change for 
Kanawana '76. 


KAMPERS 


This summer, we worked with 475 different children. The kampers 
came from many parts of Canada, the U.S., Europe and even a 
country that I've never heard of (Abu DhabI). Kanawana accepted 
children from an orphanage, Weredale House and also sponsored 
approximately 25 underprivileged children. 


Our registration surpassed our budget amount of 1225 kamper 
weeks In early June with a final total of 1356 kamper weeks 
(1264 In 1974 and 1276 in 1973). 


The returnee rate of kampers agaln Increased percentage-wise to 
46.8% from 45.2% last year as it did numerically. 


STAFF 


This season kamp had.a significant Increase of program staff 
average to 2].25 years from 19 years In 1974, 


Staff recruitment commenced in December 1974. Quite consclously, 
our returnee rate decreased from 72% last season to 52% this’ 
year. Most of Kanawana's new staff were in senlor capacities. 


! was very pleased with most of our staff but was also disappointed 
in performance of others due to their selfish attitude in working 
with other staff. This diverse minority of staff certainly did 

not help in the operations this summer and caused feelings of 
frustration wlth other staff Including myself at times. 


Staff Continued 


Most staff Individually did fine jobs In workfng with their 
kampers. The dedication and concern of these staff has enriched 
the I!Ilves of many children and certainly will be remembered for 
a lifetime. 


The organization and supervision of the four sections were wel] 

handled by our Section Directors: Judy Harper, Shella Haughton, 
Denis Basquil! and John Proctor. Their maturity and sensitivity 
made them most effective in thelr work. | sincerely thank them 

for thelr consistent dedication and co-operation throughout the 

summer. 


Stuart McLean was the Assistant Kamp Director for his second 
year. He has made an outstanding contribution to Kanawana. His 
warm outgoing personality together with his genuine Interest and 
abl lity to help people has endeared him to all who have had the 
opportunity of working with him. He has done much to contribute 
to the growth of many Kanawanians and kamp itself. I would Iike 
to express my deep appreciation to Stuart for his contribution 
and support. 


STAFF ~ ’AINING 


Our pre-kamp program was drastically changed this year from 
previous years but disappointedly was not as effective as was 
hoped. It would have been suitable for our 1974 staff but due 
to the lower returnee rate of staff this summer, [ft lacked the 
appropriate direction and structure. Notwithstanding this 
weakness, its'looseness! enabled us to more readily recognize 
difficulties in staff and deal with them accordingly. A definite 
highlight that should be continued was a two day session held 
with vartous Instructors at the Mont St. Hilaire Nature Conserv- 
ation Centre. It clearly made an impression on our staff and 
generated a real concern and awareness for our natural environ- 
ment. 


| believe that more detalled advance planning with varfous staff 
should enable us to create a relevant and appropriate training 
program for 1976. 


PROGRAM AREAS 
(For more detail, see the Assistant Kamp Director's report) 
Arts & Crafts: 


Jan Chartrand and her staff again did a fine job in this area. 
However, | do believe that we can attempt more nature crafts In 
the future. 


Sports: 


This started off well especially for the younger kampers. However, 
more planning Is required next summer. 


Jazz Dancing: 


This was a new Interest group and was well received thanks to 
Its Instructor, Sonia Barnes. It certainly should be continued. 


Nature Lore: 


Once again, we falled miserably. 1! am convinced that a very 
experienced and skilled person Is required for this very 
Important aspect of kamp. 


Musics: 


(Folk Guitar) This was popular and well received by a small 
number of kampers. 


Orienteering: 


Thanks to the maps from the Montreal Orienteering Association 
and especially to our skilled and enthustastic instructor, Gaby 
Duguay, this interest group (after attempting it since '73) grew 
In popularity very rapidly. Over 150 different kampers partici- 
pated and recelved certificates of participation. 


Drama: 


Due to interest expressed, a drama interest group was created. 
Approximately 30 different kampers participated in the prepara- 
tions and presentation of three one-act plays. 


Juntor Waterfront: 


The Instruction as well as the program was very pleasantly and 
efficiently directed for the second year in a row by Katte 
Sheahan. She, with her crew of instructors, either taught or 
helped Improve the swimming of many kampers. 


Program Areas Continued 


Sentor Waterfront: 


Unfortunately, | cannot say the same here as the Juntor Waterfront. 
The Sentor Waterfront Director was most ineffective in his methods 
of working with most other staff. The instructions went on but In 
a very uncomfortable atmosphere. After repeated attemps on my and 
Stuart's part, we were unable to initiate any Improvement and 
consequently, the Senior Waterfront Director was asked to leave 
during the fourth session of kamp. 


Hike & Trip: 


We were fortunate this summer to recruit a very experienced and 
capable Hike & Trip Director, Dick Mischook. Dick and his depart- 
ment successfully sent out a great quantity and variety of canoe 
trips, hikes and overnights. 


Due to Kanawana's past trip logs and records together with Dick's 
knowledge of trips from Powter's Camp, we were able to decrease 
the distance needed for trucking trips out and maintain the 
varlous desired wilderness experlences. 


| should also mention that Dick obtained exclusive permission for 
Kanawana to send canoe trips to Parc Jolfette. My sincere thanks 
to him for his tremendous work this summer. 


Counsellor-in-Training Program: 


Once again, our C.1.T. program has improved. Under the excellent 
direction of Lynne Robinson, the C.1.T.s were exposed to sesstons 
In group work, the history of Kanawana and the YMCA, on-the-job 
experiences, a canoe trip as well as skill training In canoeing, 
campcraft, lifesaving, etc. 


Most of the C.I.T.s are now prepared to assume staff positions 
at Kanawana and other kamps next summer. 


Some improvements are, however, needed next year and these are 
explained In Lynne's report. 


PROMOTION 


The following was the promotion program for the 1975 season. 


- 


A new brochure was developed for Kanawana, Les Voyageurs 
and C.1!.T. program as well as including all other camp 
type programs of the Montreal Y. 3,200 were distributed 
or mailed with the balance of the 7,000 produced to be 
used for 1976. 


On behalf of the Quebec Camping Association, the Kanawana 
Director was interviewed on CBC radio as well as in the 
Montreal Star and Gazette. 


Kanawana decals were given out to all registered kampers 
with their tnformation booklets. 


The kamp's bi-monthly newspaper 'The Green Triangle’ had 
four issues. 


Kanawana postcards were included with one of the Green 
Triangle issues. 


The Kanawana cartoon map idea was resurrected and. copies 
were given to all. 


Kanawana Christmas cards were sent out to former kampers 
from the last three years. 


A Kamp Kanawana reunion was held In March with attendance 
by over 200 Kanawanians. 


The Y's P.R. Department enabled brochures to be distributed 
at Eaton's among other places. 


Advertisements were placed in various local newspapers as 
well as the Gazette and Star. 


Brochures were placed in all Branches of the Montreal Y. 


HEALTH & SAFETY 


Due to our exceptionally warm weather this summer, the water 
level of the lake was down about one foot and the water temper- 
ature was up about 5° F, These factors caused a great increase 
In the bacteria count of our lake water. Consequently, we 
experienced many colds,sore throats and ear aches, etc. 


1 should add that our Nurse, Mrs. Diane Gray, did an admirable 
Job in coping with the many patients at our infirmary. 


FOOD SERVICES 


Due to the very capable supervision of Ed Neal from the Downtown 
Branch and the cooking abilities of our Head Chef, Mrs. Madeline 
Wundele, the quality and variety of hearty meals once again 
greatly Improved (as did the cost increase). 


There Is still a need for some more equipment fn the kitchen 
(i.e. mixer and exhaust fan). This will be investigated In 
greater detall this fall. 


As In 1974, we had difficulties In retaining staff in our kitchen. 
It is believed that an experienced and older staff Is required to 
avold this situation in the future. 


PHYSICAL SITE 


Some major work was done this summer but as always, it seems that 
there Is no end to It. 


Some things done were: replacing the Junior Waterfront 
" " wash areas 
- " "carwash! system 
rebuilding the walk-in fridge 
refinishing and pafnting the 
lodge and staff lounge 


Presently, there are various projects in process. There are 
numerous other pleces of work required before next summer. Some 
of these are urgently needed (i.e. septic field - girls section) 
and should be thoroughly studie¢, priorized this fall and perhaps 
some should be started by the end of September '75, 


SOME OTHER SPECIFIC RECOMMENDATIONS 


Due to the difficulty we and other camps have in relevant 
programming with 15 year olds, a two year Counsellor-in 
Training (or Leader-in-Training) program should be 
investigated along the lines of the Hami !ton Y's Camp 
Wanakita. 


In order to assist in discouraging cancellations, an 
increase of the registration deposit might be in order. 


'Mceting the Chief’ is very boring for stay-over kampers 
(and staff). This could be done at the Farmhouse next 
year during our regular change-over procedure. 


A break of perhaps 3 days. between the second and third 
session could be a feasible solutfon to many things, 
i.e. tired staff, maintenance problems, staff days off 
Interfering with interest groups and proper kamp 


operation, etc. Some sort of discussion is required. 


As canoes are constantly in need of repair, particularly 
after trips, the purchase of some kind of tripping 
canoes (perhaps fibreglass) would greatly enhance and 
assist both our tripping and in-kamp canoeing. 


Summer staff salaries must again be adjusted In order 
+o retain and attract a more competent staff. 


The feasibility of post-kamp canoe trips for Invited 
kampers should be Investigated. 


A new truck and wagon should be leased next summer. 
(The Kamp Director's car travelled over 2,000 miles 
on kamp business this summer). 


The truck could be used solely for trips while the 
wagon for various messages, emergencies or trips to 
Montreal. 


A tall conference for potential '76 staff eould be most 
useful for Kanawana tn the dsvolopment of recommend=- 
ations for our program, policies, etc. for next summer. 
Work on this should begin soon. 


CONCLUSION 


| said at the beginning of this report that | felt this was the 


best of the past three years. Although | am, in some ways 
disappotnted with this year, | still have deep feeling of respect 
and appreciation for what it is - the glories of our nature plus 


the friendship of many. 


Each staff member In doing thelr job must give much of themselves _ 
and those who give of themselves get much in return, 1 would 
l\1ke to express my personal thank to Kamp Kanawana staff ‘75. 


The two people who | work with: Julien Tasse and Olga Hall - 
my sincerest thanks for their patience, understanding and 
dedication to Kanawana - for without these two fine people, 
we would not have gone as far as we have. 


| see the future of Kanawana as very exciting. As national 
trends Indicate a loss in popularity In traditional resident 
camping, we are fortunate to maintain our registration. With 
the future plans for the Camping and Outdoor Education Branch, 
soon to become reality, | believe that we will continue to grow 
and help people grow in the same way we have been doing for 
years. 


To the future successes of Kanawanat 


Respectfully submitted, 


Derek V. Walsh, 
Director, 
Kamp Kanawana '75. 


APPRECIATION A-1 


The successes of Kamp Kanawana each summer are due to many 
different people who very generously assist us in a variety 
of ways. A sincere thanks to the following: 


Eric Smart for assisting with the setting up of 
our salling program. 


Richard (Itche) Kerr who filled In as a counsellor 
for a week when we were short. 


The Westmount, Northwestern, Downtown and Lachine- 
Dorval Branches for lending us rooms for our 
parents’ meetings. 


Ron Whittingham, our Controller, for his advice on 
financial and legal matters. 


To various O.F.Y. groups for presenting skits or 
training to us. 


Tom Thompson for obtaining a film and new postcards 
for Kamp Kanawana. 


Our seventeen Counsellors-in-Training for their 
work and assistance at Kamp this summer. 


Colin Kirk of the Montreal Orienteering Association 
for assisting with the organization of our orient- 
eering program. 


Our many neighbours who so generously permit us to 
use their property for camping. 


Dr. Bernard Villemaire for his advice on health 
matters and attending to our sick. 


Ross Bannerman, Kerry Johnston and Tom Potts for 
their guidance and advice on many aspects of kamp. 


The staff of the Montreel YMCA for their continued 
encouragement and co-operation. 


The Kanawana Committee and the Branch Board of 
Management for their hundreds of hours of work in 
preparing Kamp Kanawana '75. 


THANKS AGAIN

GOD'S BACK YARD 


Close your eyes and think real hard 
Imagine kamp as God's back yard. 

The grass so green, the hills so tall 
Close your eyes and think of all 

The beauty of our life at kamp, 

The morning sun on the grass so damp. 
Flags in a circle from countries brave 
Close your eyes and see them wave. 


Children together and children apart 

Some grown up and some ready to start. 

Can you picture your cabin or a favorite tree? 
Close your eyes and try to see 

The sounds of night time,dark and still 

The laughter from a far away hill. 

Remember the good times with friends old and new. 
Take all of these memories home with you. 

Yes, we've worked together and played so hard, 

At Kanawana, in God's back yard. 


eseeeed0an Dalrymple
